groups.title: Nuxt Module System
groups.question: Your team repeats the same setup across several Nuxt apps and wants to use community modules for auth and images. Explain how modules work and how to choose them.

followUps.Building Custom Nuxt Modules: What does a custom Nuxt module do and when does it run?
followUps.Using Community Modules Safely: What should you check before adding a community module?

evidence.text: A module is created with defineNuxtModule.
It can add plugins, components and auto-imports.
Modules run at build time to configure the app.
Check that it is maintained and compatible with your Nuxt version.
Modules add config, plugins and code to your app.
Each one adds dependencies and possible bundle size.

groups.title: Advanced Vue Patterns
groups.question: You need a table component that builds its columns from data, and a modal that escapes a parent with overflow hidden. Explain render functions and Teleport.

followUps.Render Functions and JSX in Vue 3: When would you use a render function instead of a template?
followUps.Teleport for Portal Rendering: What does Teleport solve for a modal?

evidence.text: Render functions build the UI in JavaScript with h() or JSX.
They suit highly dynamic structures that templates express poorly.
Templates are easier to read and get compiler optimisations, so render functions are the exception.
Teleport renders its content in a different DOM location, like the body.
This escapes parent styles like overflow hidden or z-index stacking.
The component keeps its logical place and state in the tree.

groups.title: TypeScript Advanced Patterns
groups.question: You want your API helper's return type to depend on the endpoint, and a plugin adds a $api helper that TypeScript does not know about. Explain the advanced types you would use.

followUps.Conditional Types and Template Literals: How do conditional and template literal types make types more precise?
followUps.Declaration Merging and Module Augmentat: How do you tell TypeScript about a property a plugin adds?

evidence.text: Conditional types choose a type based on another type.
Template literal types build string types from patterns.
Together they give precise return types based on inputs, like an endpoint string.
Module augmentation extends an existing type declaration.
Plugins augment the NuxtApp type to add their helpers.
Without it, the helper is untyped or reported as missing.

notEnough: Only saying you extend the type.

groups.title: Nuxt Hooks and Lifecycle
groups.question: You want to track page view timing at runtime and modify the build output. Explain Nuxt's hook systems and how code accesses the app instance.

followUps.App Hooks vs Build Hooks: What is the difference between app hooks and build hooks?

evidence.text: App hooks run at runtime, like when a page finishes loading.
Build hooks run while building the app.
Page view tracking uses app hooks; changing build output uses build hooks.
useNuxtApp returns the shared Nuxt app instance.
It gives access to provided helpers, hooks and the SSR payload.
It must be called within Nuxt's context, like in setup or plugins.

notEnough: Only saying it returns the app.
